concepts.title: The passive with essere and venire
concepts.rule: The passive is essere or venire + past participle agreeing with the subject; the agent takes da (dal, dalla…). Venire is only possible in simple tenses (viene, veniva, verrà, venne), never in compound ones (è stato fatto, not è venuto fatto).
assessment: Forms the passive with essere in any tense, with the participle agreeing with the subject
Uses venire as the auxiliary in simple tenses only, and essere in compound tenses
Introduces the agent with da and its combined forms (dal, dalla, dagli…)
Turns active sentences into passive ones (and back) keeping the same tense
Avoids the English 'I was given…' structure, using mi è stato dato… instead

lesson.intro: Italian news, reports and formal writing use the passive constantly, and it works much like English: the object becomes the subject. Two things trip English speakers up. First, Italian has **two** auxiliaries, *essere* and *venire*, and *venire* is forbidden in compound tenses. Second, 'by' is **da**, never *per*. Get these right and your written Italian immediately sounds more controlled.

rules.title: Form: essere + past participle
rules.text: Conjugate *essere* in the tense of the active verb and add the past participle, which **agrees** with the new subject in gender and number. The tense of the passive always matches the tense of the active sentence.

examples.it: Il sindaco inaugura la mostra. → La mostra **è inaugurata** dal sindaco.
examples.en: The mayor opens the exhibition. → The exhibition is opened by the mayor.

examples.it: Hanno venduto la casa. → La casa **è stata venduta**.
examples.en: They sold the house. → The house was sold.

examples.it: I ladri **saranno arrestati** presto.
examples.en: The thieves will be arrested soon.

rules.title: Venire: only in simple tenses
rules.text: *Venire* can replace *essere* in **simple** tenses (presente, imperfetto, futuro, passato remoto, condizionale presente, congiuntivo presente/imperfetto). It stresses the **action** rather than the resulting state. In **compound** tenses only *essere* is possible: ~~è venuto costruito~~ → *è stato costruito*.

examples.it: Le porte **vengono chiuse** alle 20.
examples.en: The doors are closed (= someone closes them) at 8 pm.

examples.it: Le porte **sono chiuse**.
examples.en: The doors are closed (state, or action: ambiguous).

examples.it: Il ponte **venne costruito** nel 1950. / Il ponte **è stato costruito** nel 1950.
examples.en: The bridge was built in 1950.

rules.title: The agent: da, not per
rules.text: The person or thing doing the action is introduced by **da**, which combines with the article: *dal, dallo, dalla, dall', dai, dagli, dalle*. *Per* means 'for' or 'through' and never marks the agent.

examples.it: Il quadro è stato dipinto **da** Caravaggio.
examples.en: The painting was painted by Caravaggio.

examples.it: Il progetto è stato approvato **dagli** azionisti.
examples.en: The project was approved by the shareholders.

rules.title: 'I was given…': Italian can't passivise the indirect object
rules.text: English turns the person receiving into the subject ('I was given a book'). Italian can't: only the **direct object** can become the subject. Keep the person as an indirect object pronoun: *Mi è stato dato un libro*, or simply use the active *Mi hanno dato un libro*.

examples.it: **Mi è stato offerto** un lavoro a Milano.
examples.en: I was offered a job in Milan.

examples.it: **Ai vincitori sono stati consegnati** i premi.
examples.en: The winners were given the prizes.

rules.title: Passive after modal verbs
rules.text: With *dovere, potere, volere* the modal is conjugated and the passive infinitive follows: *deve essere firmato, può essere usato*. In compound tenses: *avrebbe dovuto essere firmato*.

examples.it: Il contratto **deve essere firmato** entro venerdì.
examples.en: The contract must be signed by Friday.

mistakes.wrong: La chiesa è venuta costruita nel Trecento.
mistakes.right: La chiesa è stata costruita nel Trecento.
mistakes.why: *Venire* can't be used in compound tenses. Use *essere stato*, or the passato remoto *venne costruita*.

mistakes.wrong: Il libro è stato scritto per Umberto Eco.
mistakes.right: Il libro è stato scritto da Umberto Eco.
mistakes.why: The agent is introduced by *da*. *Per Umberto Eco* would mean 'for Umberto Eco'.

mistakes.right: Mi è stato dato un regalo.
mistakes.why: Only the direct object (*un regalo*) can become the subject. The person stays as an indirect object: *mi*.
In the passive, both *stato* and the participle agree with the subject: *la casa → stata venduta*.

tips: Quick check for *venire*: if the verb form has *stato* in it, *venire* is impossible.
Use *venire* when you want to make clear that something is being done, not that it's in a state: *Il negozio viene chiuso* (someone closes it) vs *Il negozio è chiuso* (it's shut).
Newspaper headlines and reports love the passato remoto passive: *venne arrestato, fu scoperto*. Recognise it even if you prefer the passato prossimo when speaking.

exercises.prompt: Il ponte ___ (costruire) nel 1950.

traps.why: *Venire* can't form compound tenses. Passato prossimo passive = *è stato* + participle.
*Stato* goes with *essere*: *è stato costruito*.
That's active ('it built'). The bridge didn't build anything: it *was built*, *è stato costruito*.

exercises.explanation: Passato prossimo passive = *essere* (passato prossimo: *è stato*) + participle agreeing with *il ponte*: **è stato costruito**.
exercises.en: The bridge was built in 1950.

exercises.prompt: Ogni anno il festival ___ (organizzare) dal Comune.

traps.why: The festival is the thing organised, not the organiser: passive *è / viene organizzato*.
The participle agrees with *il festival* (masculine): *organizzato*.

exercises.explanation: Present passive: *è organizzato* or *viene organizzato*. Both work in a simple tense; *viene* stresses the yearly action.
exercises.en: Every year the festival is organised by the town council.

exercises.prompt: Le lettere ___ (spedire) domani mattina.

traps.why: *Le lettere* is feminine plural, so the participle is *spedite*.
*Spediranno* is active ('they will send'). With *le lettere* as subject you need the passive: *saranno / verranno spedite*.

exercises.explanation: Future passive: *saranno spedite* or *verranno spedite*. The participle agrees with *le lettere*.
exercises.en: The letters will be sent tomorrow morning.

exercises.prompt: Finora questo romanzo ___ tradotto in venti lingue.

optionWhy.0: *Venire* can't be used in compound tenses: *è stato tradotto*.
optionWhy.3: *Finora* ('so far') needs the passato prossimo, not the present.

exercises.explanation: *Finora* → passato prossimo, and the passato prossimo passive is only possible with *essere*: **è stato tradotto**.
exercises.en: So far this novel has been translated into twenty languages.

exercises.prompt: La Gioconda è stata dipinta ___ Leonardo.

traps.why: 'By' in a passive is *da*. *Per Leonardo* means 'for Leonardo'.
*Di Leonardo* means 'Leonardo's' (possession). The agent takes *da*.

exercises.explanation: The agent of a passive is introduced by **da**.
exercises.en: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.

exercises.instruction: Which form makes it clear this is a repeated action, not a state?
exercises.prompt: Ogni sera alle 20 le porte del museo ___ dal custode.

optionWhy.1: *Sono chiuse* can also describe a state ('they are shut'). *Venire* removes the ambiguity.
optionWhy.2: *Sono state chiuse* is a one-off past action, which doesn't fit *ogni sera*.

exercises.explanation: *Venire* in a simple tense stresses the action: **vengono chiuse** = someone closes them every evening.
exercises.en: Every evening at 8 the museum doors are closed by the caretaker.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite in the passive, keeping the agent.
exercises.prompt: Il sindaco ha inaugurato la nuova biblioteca.
answers: La nuova biblioteca è stata inaugurata dal sindaco

traps.why: Passato prossimo → only *essere*: *è stata inaugurata*.
The new subject is *la biblioteca* (feminine): *stata inaugurata*.
The agent takes *da* (+ article → *dal sindaco*).

exercises.explanation: Same tense (passato prossimo) → *è stata inaugurata*; agent with *dal*.
exercises.en: The new library was opened by the mayor.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite in the passive, keeping the agent and the tense.
exercises.prompt: La polizia arresterà i ladri.

traps.why: *I ladri* is masculine plural: *arrestati*.
The active verb is future (*arresterà*), so the passive is future too: *saranno / verranno arrestati*.

exercises.explanation: Future → *saranno* or *verranno arrestati*; agent *dalla polizia*.
exercises.en: The thieves will be arrested by the police.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite in the passive, keeping the agent and the tense.
exercises.prompt: Gli studenti leggevano questi libri.

traps.why: *Da* combines with the article: *da + gli = dagli*.
Keep the imperfetto: *erano / venivano letti*.
*Questi libri* → *letti*.

exercises.explanation: Imperfetto → *erano* or *venivano letti*; *da + gli* → **dagli**.
exercises.en: These books were read by the students.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian using the passive.
exercises.prompt: The window was broken by the children.
answers: La finestra è stata rotta dai (bambini|ragazzi)

traps.why: No *venire* in compound tenses: *è stata rotta* (or passato remoto *venne rotta*).
'By' = *da*: *dai bambini*.
*La finestra* is feminine: *rotta*.
*Era rotta* describes a state ('was broken', already). The agent shows an action: *è stata rotta dai bambini*.

exercises.explanation: A single past action: *è stata rotta* (or the written *fu / venne rotta*), agent *dai bambini*.
exercises.en: The window was broken by the children.

exercises.prompt: I was given a present.

traps.why: Italian can't make the receiver the subject. The present is the subject: *Mi è stato dato un regalo*.
The subject is *un regalo* (masculine), so *stato dato*.

exercises.explanation: The direct object (*un regalo*) becomes the subject; the person stays as indirect object *mi*: **Mi è stato dato un regalo** (or active *Mi hanno dato…*).
exercises.en: I was given a present.

exercises.prompt: Mi hanno detto che la riunione ___ (rimandare) a lunedì.

traps.why: The trapassato is a compound tense, so *venire* isn't possible: *era stata rimandata*.
*La riunione* is feminine: *stata rimandata*.
The passive uses *essere* throughout: *era stata*.

exercises.explanation: Trapassato passive: *era stata* + participle, all agreeing with *la riunione*.
exercises.en: They told me the meeting had been postponed to Monday.

exercises.prompt: The contract will be signed by the director.
answers: Il contratto verrà firmato dal direttore
exercises.explanation: Subject + passive verb (*verrà firmato*) + agent (*dal direttore*), as in English.

exercises.prompt: Si dice che l'edificio ___ progettato da Renzo Piano.

optionWhy.1: The congiuntivo passato is compound, so *venire* is impossible.

exercises.explanation: *Si dice che* + congiuntivo; a past passive → **sia stato progettato**.
exercises.en: They say the building was designed by Renzo Piano.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian, using the passive.
exercises.prompt: Tell a visitor that the cathedral was built in the 14th century.
answers: La cattedrale (è stata|fu|venne) costruita nel (Trecento|quattordicesimo secolo|XIV secolo)

traps.why: No *venire* in compound tenses: *è stata costruita* (or *venne costruita*).
*La cattedrale* is feminine: *costruita*.

exercises.explanation: *La cattedrale è stata costruita nel Trecento*. Italians often name centuries as *il Trecento* (= the 1300s).
exercises.en: The cathedral was built in the 14th century.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite in the active, keeping the tense.
exercises.prompt: Il premio venne consegnato al vincitore dal presidente.
answers: Il presidente consegnò il premio al vincitore

traps.why: *Venne consegnato* is passato remoto, so the active is *consegnò*, not the passato prossimo.
In the active there's no participle: the passato remoto of *consegnare* is *consegnò*.

exercises.explanation: The agent (*dal presidente*) becomes the subject; *venne consegnato* (passato remoto) → **consegnò**.
exercises.en: The president presented the prize to the winner.

concepts.title: The passive with andare (va fatto) and obligation
concepts.rule: Andare + past participle means 'must be done' (va fatto = deve essere fatto; andrebbe fatto = should be done) and only works in simple tenses. With verbs of loss (perdere, smarrire, sprecare, distruggere) andare is a plain passive with no obligation, and compound tenses are fine: è andato perso.
assessment: Uses va / vanno + participle to express obligation, with correct agreement
Uses andrebbe / andrebbero + participle for recommendations ('should be…')
Avoids andare-obligation in compound tenses, using andava or doveva essere instead
Uses andare perso / smarrito / sprecato as a plain passive, including in compound tenses
Recognises formal set phrases like va detto che, va ricordato che, non va dimenticato che

lesson.intro: Instructions, labels and formal texts are full of *va fatto*, *vanno rispettate*, *andrebbe detto*. This passive with *andare* packs 'must be' into one word, and it has no English equivalent, so learners often avoid it or misread it. There's a second, completely different use: *andare perso* ('to get lost'), which has no idea of obligation at all.

rules.title: Andare + participle = must be (obligation)
rules.text: *Andare* conjugated + past participle = *dovere essere* + participle. The participle agrees with the subject. The agent is normally left out: the point is the duty, not who does it.

examples.it: Questo modulo **va compilato** in stampatello.
examples.en: This form must be filled in in block capitals.

examples.it: Le medicine **vanno prese** dopo i pasti.
examples.en: The medicine must be taken after meals.

examples.it: Le scarpe **vanno tolte** all'ingresso.
examples.en: Shoes must be removed at the entrance.

rules.title: Andrebbe = should be (softer advice)
rules.text: The conditional turns the obligation into a recommendation or criticism: *andrebbe fatto* = 'it should be done', *andrebbe detto* = 'it should be said'. In the past, use *andava* ('had to be') or *sarebbe dovuto essere* ('should have been').

examples.it: La questione **andrebbe affrontata** con più calma.
examples.en: The matter should be dealt with more calmly.

examples.it: Il lavoro **andava finito** entro le cinque.
examples.en: The work had to be finished by five.

rules.title: Only simple tenses for obligation
rules.text: Like *venire*, obligation-*andare* can't appear in compound tenses: ~~è andato fatto~~. For a past obligation use *andava fatto* or *doveva essere fatto*.

examples.it: Quel documento **andava firmato** ieri.
examples.en: That document had to be signed yesterday.

rules.title: Andare + verbs of loss: a plain passive
rules.text: With *perdere, smarrire, sprecare, distruggere, dimenticare* (and a few others), *andare* means 'to get / end up' + participle. There's **no** obligation, and compound tenses are normal: *è andato perso* = 'it got lost'.

examples.it: Il mio bagaglio **è andato smarrito**.
examples.en: My luggage got lost.

examples.it: Tutto il cibo avanzato **è andato sprecato**.
examples.en: All the leftover food went to waste.

examples.it: Molti documenti **andarono distrutti** nell'incendio.
examples.en: Many documents were destroyed in the fire.

rules.title: Set phrases in formal writing
rules.text: *Va detto che…* ('it must be said that'), *va ricordato che…*, *va sottolineato che…*, *non va dimenticato che…*. They introduce a point in essays and reports and are followed by the **indicative** when stating a fact.

examples.it: **Va detto** che i risultati sono incoraggianti.
examples.en: It must be said that the results are encouraging.

mistakes.wrong: Il lavoro è andato fatto ieri.
mistakes.right: Il lavoro andava fatto ieri. / Il lavoro doveva essere fatto ieri.
mistakes.why: Obligation-*andare* only works in simple tenses.
*Andare* agrees with the subject (*questi errori* → *vanno*), and so does the participle.
*Andare* takes the past participle, not the infinitive.
For something that got lost, use the passato prossimo: with verbs of loss *andare* is an ordinary passive and compound tenses are fine.

tips: Read *va* + participle as 'must be': *va fatto* = must be done. With *perso / smarrito / sprecato* read it as 'got': *è andato perso* = got lost.
*Andrebbe detto che…* is a polite way to add a criticism in a meeting.
Look for *va / vanno* on labels and instructions: *da consumarsi*, *va conservato in frigorifero*, *non va ingerito*.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of andare (present).
exercises.prompt: Questo modulo ___ compilato in stampatello.

traps.why: *Questo modulo* is singular: *va*.

exercises.explanation: *Va compilato* = *deve essere compilato*: obligation.
exercises.en: This form must be filled in in block capitals.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of andare (present).
exercises.prompt: Le medicine ___ prese dopo i pasti.

traps.why: *Andare* agrees with the subject *le medicine* (plural): *vanno*.

exercises.explanation: Plural subject → **vanno prese** ('must be taken').
exercises.en: The medicine must be taken after meals.

exercises.prompt: Il latte deve essere conservato in frigorifero.
answers: Il latte va conservato in frigorifero

traps.why: *Andare* takes the past participle: *va conservato*.
No *essere* needed: *va conservato* already means 'must be kept'.

exercises.explanation: *Deve essere conservato* → **va conservato**.
exercises.en: Milk must be kept in the fridge.

exercises.prompt: Questi errori devono essere corretti subito.

traps.why: Plural subject (*questi errori*) → *vanno*.
*Andare* + past participle: *corretti*, not the infinitive.
The participle agrees with *errori*: *corretti*.

exercises.explanation: *Devono essere corretti* → **vanno corretti**.
exercises.en: These mistakes must be corrected immediately.

exercises.instruction: Complete with andare in the conditional ('should be').
exercises.prompt: Secondo me, la questione ___ affrontata con più calma.

traps.why: *Va affrontata* is a firm obligation ('must be'). *Secondo me* signals advice: conditional *andrebbe*.
*La questione* is singular: *andrebbe*.

exercises.explanation: Conditional *andrebbe* + participle = 'should be' (recommendation).
exercises.en: In my view, the matter should be dealt with more calmly.

exercises.prompt: Il pacco ___ perso durante il trasloco.

optionWhy.2: *Va perso* is present ('gets lost'), but the move is over.

exercises.explanation: With verbs of loss, *andare* is an ordinary passive and compound tenses are fine: **è andato perso** = it got lost.
exercises.en: The parcel got lost during the move.

exercises.prompt: Questo vino va bevuto fresco.
options: This wine must be drunk chilled.
This wine is being drunk chilled.
This wine went off when chilled.
exercises.explanation: *Va* + participle = obligation: 'must be drunk'.
exercises.en: This wine must be drunk chilled.

exercises.prompt: Ieri quel lavoro ___ fatto entro le cinque.

optionWhy.1: Obligation-*andare* can't be used in compound tenses: *è andato fatto* is wrong. Use *andava fatto*.

exercises.explanation: Past obligation with *andare* → imperfetto: **andava fatto** ('had to be done'). Compound tenses aren't possible.
exercises.en: Yesterday that work had to be done by five.

exercises.prompt: It must be said that the results are good.
answers: Va detto che i risultati sono (buoni|positivi)

match: (Bisogna|Si deve) dire che i risultati sono (buoni|positivi)
Deve essere detto che i risultati sono (buoni|positivi)
traps.why: Correct Italian. The more compact formal version is *Va detto che…*.
*Va detto che* introduces a fact, so the indicative *sono* is right.
*Andare* takes the past participle: *va detto*.

exercises.explanation: *Va detto che…* = 'it must be said that…', a typical formal opener.
exercises.en: It must be said that the results are good.

exercises.prompt: My luggage got lost.

traps.why: Correct, but *è andato perso / smarrito* is the natural way to say something 'got lost'.
*Andare* takes *essere*: *è andato*.
*Il bagaglio* is masculine: *perso / smarrito*.

exercises.explanation: With verbs of loss, *andare* + participle = 'get lost', in any tense: **è andato smarrito**.
exercises.en: My luggage got lost.

exercises.prompt: Bisogna ricordare che il progetto è ancora in fase sperimentale.
answers: Va ricordato che il progetto è ancora in fase sperimentale

traps.why: *Andare* + past participle: *va ricordato*.
The fact stays in the indicative: *è ancora in fase sperimentale*.

exercises.explanation: *Bisogna ricordare che* → **Va ricordato che**: same meaning, more compact and formal.
exercises.en: It should be remembered that the project is still at an experimental stage.

exercises.instruction: Complete with andare in the passato prossimo.
exercises.prompt: Tutto il cibo avanzato ___ sprecato.

traps.why: *È stato andato* doesn't exist: *è andato sprecato*.
*Andare* takes *essere*.
The prompt asks for the passato prossimo: *è andato*.

exercises.explanation: *Andare sprecato* ('go to waste'): verb of loss, so the compound tense is fine: **è andato sprecato**.
exercises.en: All the leftover food went to waste.

exercises.prompt: Shoes must be removed at the entrance.
exercises.explanation: *Vanno tolte* = must be removed; the participle agrees with *le scarpe*.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian, using andare + participle.
exercises.prompt: Tell a new colleague that this document should be signed by tomorrow (a recommendation).

traps.why: Correct, but *va* is a firm 'must'. For 'should', use the conditional *andrebbe*.
*Andare* + past participle: *firmato*.

exercises.explanation: 'Should be signed' → conditional **andrebbe firmato**.
exercises.en: This document should be signed by tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: Find the ungrammatical sentence.
options: La lettera è andata spedita ieri.

optionWhy.3: Correct: verbs of loss allow compound tenses.

exercises.explanation: Obligation-*andare* can't be used in compound tenses: ~~è andata spedita~~. Say *andava spedita* or *è stata spedita*. Only verbs of loss (*è andata persa*) allow it.
exercises.en: Which sentence is wrong?

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using andare + past participle (keep the conditional).
exercises.prompt: Si dovrebbero ridurre i costi.

traps.why: *I costi* is plural: *andrebbero*.
The participle agrees with *i costi*: *ridotti*.
*Andare* + past participle: *ridotti*.

exercises.explanation: The object *i costi* becomes the subject: **I costi andrebbero ridotti** ('costs should be cut').
exercises.en: Costs should be cut.

concepts.title: Si passivante vs si impersonale
concepts.rule: Si + verb with a direct object is passive: the verb agrees with the object (si vende una casa, si vendono case). Without a direct object si is impersonal and the verb is singular, but adjectives are plural (si è felici). Reflexive verbs become ci si (ci si alza). Compound tenses always take essere: si sono vendute, si è mangiato, si è partiti.
assessment: Makes the verb agree with the plural object after si passivante (si vendono, si devono rispettare)
Uses si impersonale with a singular verb and plural adjectives (si è stanchi)
Uses ci si with reflexive verbs (ci si alza, ci si diverte)
Forms compound tenses with essere and the correct participle ending (si sono vendute, si è mangiato, si è partiti)
Uses si for generic 'you / one / people' instead of tu or la gente

lesson.intro: Where English says 'you', 'one', 'people' or 'they' for people in general, Italian uses *si*. It's everywhere: signs, recipes, rules, conversation. The traps are agreement: *si vendono case*, not ~~si vende case~~; *si è stanchi*, not ~~si è stanco~~; and the reflexive form *ci si*, which has no English parallel.

rules.title: Si passivante: the verb agrees with the object
rules.text: With a transitive verb and a direct object, *si* works like a passive: the object is really the subject, so the verb agrees with it. Singular object → singular verb; plural object → plural verb. The same goes for modals: *si devono rispettare le regole*.

examples.it: **Si vende** casa con giardino.
examples.en: House with garden for sale.

examples.it: In questo negozio **si vendono** solo prodotti biologici.
examples.en: This shop only sells organic products.

examples.it: **Si devono rispettare** le regole.
examples.en: The rules must be respected.

rules.title: Si impersonale: singular verb, plural adjectives
rules.text: Without a direct object (intransitive verbs, or *essere*, *diventare*…), *si* means 'one / people / you'. The verb is always **singular**, but adjectives and nouns referring to the people are **plural**.

examples.it: In Italia **si mangia** bene.
examples.en: You eat well in Italy.

examples.it: Quando **si è giovani**, si pensa di poter fare tutto.
examples.en: When you're young, you think you can do anything.

examples.it: **Si parla** molto di questo film.
examples.en: People are talking a lot about this film.

rules.title: Reflexive verbs: ci si
rules.text: A reflexive verb already has *si* (*alzarsi*), and Italian can't say ~~si si~~. The impersonal becomes **ci si**: *ci si alza*, *ci si diverte*, *ci si annoia*.

examples.it: In vacanza **ci si alza** tardi.
examples.en: On holiday you get up late.

examples.it: Quando si è stanchi **ci si annoia** facilmente.
examples.en: When you're tired, you get bored easily.

rules.title: Compound tenses: always essere
rules.text: All *si* constructions take **essere** in compound tenses. The participle depends on the type: si passivante → agrees with the object; si impersonale with a verb that normally takes *avere* → **-o**; with a verb that normally takes *essere* (including reflexives) → **-i** (masculine plural).

rules.title: Si with other pronouns
rules.text: Object pronouns go **before** *si*: *lo si fa, la si vede*. With *ne* the *si* becomes *se*: *se ne parla* ('people talk about it').

examples.it: Di questo problema **se ne parla** da anni.
examples.en: People have been talking about this problem for years.

examples.it: Il vino buono **lo si riconosce** subito.
examples.en: You recognise good wine straight away.

mistakes.wrong: Si vende biglietti per il concerto.
mistakes.right: Si vendono biglietti per il concerto.
mistakes.why: *Biglietti* is the real subject (plural), so the verb is plural.

mistakes.wrong: Quando si è stanco si lavora male.
mistakes.right: Quando si è stanchi si lavora male.
mistakes.why: With si impersonale, adjectives are plural.

mistakes.wrong: In vacanza si si alza tardi.
mistakes.right: In vacanza ci si alza tardi.

mistakes.wrong: Alla festa si ha ballato molto.
mistakes.right: Alla festa si è ballato molto.
mistakes.why: All *si* constructions take *essere* in compound tenses.

mistakes.wrong: Qui non puoi fumare. (on a sign)
mistakes.right: Qui non si può fumare. / Vietato fumare.
mistakes.why: For general rules, Italian uses impersonal *si*, not *tu*.

tips: Test: is there a direct object after the verb? Yes → make the verb agree with it. No → singular verb.
Think of *si è* + plural adjective as 'one is' + 'people': *si è contenti*.
*Ci si* is just the reflexive *si* plus impersonal *si* in disguise: *ci si vede!* ('see you!') is the same structure.

exercises.instruction: Complete with si + the verb in the present.
exercises.prompt: In questo negozio ___ (vendere) solo prodotti biologici.

traps.why: *Prodotti* is plural and is the real subject: *si vendono*. *Si vende prodotti* is common in speech but non-standard.
Without *si* this means 'they sell'. The general 'is sold / are sold' needs *si vendono*.

exercises.explanation: Si passivante: the verb agrees with the plural object → **si vendono**.
exercises.en: This shop only sells organic products.

exercises.instruction: Complete with si + the verb in the present.
exercises.prompt: In Italia ___ (mangiare) la pasta quasi ogni giorno.

traps.why: *La pasta* is singular: *si mangia*.

exercises.explanation: Singular object (*la pasta*) → singular verb: **si mangia**.
exercises.en: In Italy people eat pasta almost every day.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the impersonal form of the reflexive verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: In vacanza ___ (alzarsi) sempre tardi.

traps.why: Two *si* can't follow each other: reflexive + impersonal → *ci si alza*.
*Si alza* means 'he / she gets up'. The impersonal 'you / people get up' is *ci si alza*.
Si impersonale takes a singular verb: *ci si alza*.

exercises.explanation: Reflexive verb + impersonal *si* → **ci si alza**.
exercises.en: On holiday you always get up late.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the adjective.
exercises.prompt: Quando si è ___ (stanco), si lavora male.

traps.why: After impersonal *si*, adjectives are plural: *si è stanchi*.
Impersonal *si* takes a masculine plural adjective: *stanchi*.

exercises.explanation: Si impersonale: singular verb (*si è*) but plural adjective: **stanchi**.
exercises.en: When you're tired, you work badly.

exercises.prompt: Ieri ___ molti biglietti per il concerto.

optionWhy.1: *Biglietti* is plural and the real subject: *si sono venduti*.
optionWhy.3: Verb and participle both agree with *biglietti*: *si sono venduti*.

exercises.explanation: Si passivante in the passato prossimo: *essere* + participle, both agreeing with the object: **si sono venduti**.
exercises.en: Yesterday a lot of tickets were sold for the concert.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the impersonal form in the passato prossimo.
exercises.prompt: Alla festa ___ (divertirsi) moltissimo.

traps.why: Reflexive verbs with impersonal *si* take a plural participle: *divertiti*.
*Divertirsi* is reflexive, so the impersonal is *ci si*: *ci si è divertiti*.
*Si* constructions always take *essere*.

exercises.explanation: Reflexive → *ci si*; compound tense → *è*; essere-type verb → participle in **-i**: *ci si è divertiti*.
exercises.en: We all had a great time at the party.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the impersonal form in the passato prossimo.
exercises.prompt: A quella cena ___ (mangiare) benissimo.

traps.why: Even verbs that normally take *avere* switch to *essere* with *si*: *si è mangiato*.
There's no object, and *mangiare* normally takes *avere*, so the participle stays in *-o*: *si è mangiato*.

exercises.explanation: Si impersonale + verb that normally takes *avere* → *si è* + participle in **-o**.
exercises.en: We ate wonderfully at that dinner.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the impersonal form in the passato prossimo.
exercises.prompt: Quella volta ___ (partire) all'alba per evitare il traffico.

traps.why: *Partire* normally takes *essere*, so with impersonal *si* the participle is plural: *si è partiti*.
*Si* constructions always take *essere*.

exercises.explanation: Essere-verb + impersonal *si* → participle in **-i**: *si è partiti*.
exercises.en: That time we set off at dawn to avoid the traffic.

exercises.prompt: La gente parla molto di questo film.
answers: Si parla molto di questo film
Di questo film si parla molto

traps.why: *Di questo film* isn't a direct object, so the verb stays singular: *si parla*.

exercises.explanation: No direct object → si impersonale, singular verb: **si parla**.
exercises.en: People are talking a lot about this film.

exercises.prompt: In questo ufficio rispettiamo le regole.
answers: In questo ufficio si rispettano le regole
In questo ufficio le regole si rispettano

traps.why: *Le regole* is plural and is the real subject: *si rispettano*.

exercises.explanation: Si passivante with a plural object → **si rispettano**.
exercises.en: In this office the rules are respected.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using si (keep the passato prossimo).
exercises.prompt: Abbiamo costruito molte case nuove.
answers: Si sono costruite molte case nuove

traps.why: With si passivante the participle agrees with the object *case* (feminine plural): *costruite*.
*Case* is feminine: *costruite*.
*Si* constructions take *essere*: *si sono costruite*.
The verb agrees with the plural object: *si sono*.

exercises.explanation: Si passivante, compound tense: *essere* + participle agreeing with *molte case* → **si sono costruite**.
exercises.en: Many new houses have been built.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (a general rule, not addressed to one person).
exercises.prompt: You can't smoke here.

traps.why: For a general rule Italian uses impersonal *si*: *non si può fumare*.
Also correct (a sign-style ban). The *si* version is: *Qui non si può fumare*.

exercises.explanation: Generic 'you' → impersonal **si**: *Qui non si può fumare* (or *non si fuma*).
exercises.en: You can't smoke here.

exercises.prompt: When one is tired, one gets bored easily.
answers: Quando si è stanchi[,] ci si annoia (facilmente|con facilità)
Ci si annoia (facilmente|con facilità) quando si è stanchi

traps.why: Impersonal *si* takes a plural adjective: *si è stanchi*.

traps.match: Quando si è stanchi si annoia (facilmente|con facilità)
traps.why: *Annoiarsi* is reflexive, so the impersonal is *ci si annoia*.
'One' is translated with impersonal *si*, not *uno*, in neutral Italian.

exercises.explanation: *Si è* + plural adjective (*stanchi*), and reflexive *annoiarsi* → **ci si annoia**.
exercises.en: When one is tired, one gets bored easily.

exercises.prompt: Three languages are spoken here.
exercises.explanation: *Si* + verb agreeing with the plural object *tre lingue*: *si parlano*.

exercises.prompt: Le regole ___ rispettare sempre.

optionWhy.1: *Si deve rispettare le regole* is heard in speech, but in standard Italian the modal agrees with the plural object: *si devono rispettare*.
optionWhy.2: *Ci si* is only for reflexive verbs; *rispettare* isn't reflexive here.

exercises.explanation: With si passivante + modal, the modal agrees with the object: *le regole* → **si devono**.
exercises.en: Rules must always be respected.

exercises.prompt: Ask how you say 'deadline' in Italian.
answers: Come si dice deadline in italiano

traps.why: The question is general, not about one person: *Come si dice…?*

exercises.explanation: *Come si dice…?* is the classic impersonal *si*. (The answer is *scadenza*.)
exercises.en: How do you say 'deadline' in Italian?

exercises.prompt: Di questo problema ___ è parlato a lungo.

optionWhy.3: *Ci si* is for reflexive verbs; here we need *ne* for 'about it'.

exercises.explanation: *Si* + *ne* → **se ne** (*se n'è parlato*), just like *me ne, te ne*.
exercises.en: This problem was discussed at length.
